# OpenDevGuild 0.4.0

Public development pre-release: reviewed procedures and tested tooling, with explicit client and evaluation limits.

## What changed

- Preserved all 42 skills and 8 optional Codex profiles; audited each against 18 documented criteria.
- Added beginner installation/quick-start guides in English and Spanish, troubleshooting, compatibility and eight usage scenarios.
- Added optional local selective install/update/uninstall/rollback, dry-run plans, hash-based user-change protection and bounded recovery history.
- Added bounded provenance registry with L0–L4 evidence gates, revision-aware deduplication and reproducible stratified sampling.
- Mapped 36 adjacent responsibilities and supplied 8 on-demand procedures rather than creating 36 new skills.
- Added native checksum/public-download verification on Linux, Windows and macOS.

Manual users do not need Python, uv or contributor dependencies. Choose one or two skills and copy the folders to the actual documented client discovery path. Do not overwrite existing skills. Optional subagent profiles are separate and do not grant permissions.

## Evidence

Source commit: 6abd610afaaa376c014aad409723fc976fd721f4.
[Pre-release CI 42554540018](https://github.com/kkshiiit/opendevguild/actions/runs/42554540018) passed Linux/Python3.11 and3.12, Windows/Python3.12, macOS/Python3.12 and actual Chromium execution. Literal copy/collision recipes were exercised on native platforms. The local complete suite ran 110 methods: 109 passed and 1 PowerShell case was unavailable locally; platformCI tests it separately. Original failed Windows checksum invocation was corrected, not suppressed.

Two local builds were byte-identical. The extracted ZIP passed project/visual validators and clean-target install, collision, modified-user-file rejection, update, uninstall and rollback checks. No Git history, environment, local database or temp data is included.

`opendevguild-0.4.0.zip` SHA-256:

```
d44f69effd2ea8c3784352006b8fdc8d40e1ac384d4cfb6b5c6affd2d9191a4a
```

Download both ZIP and `.zip.sha256`. Check with `sha256sum -c` onLinux, `shasum -a256 -c` onmacOS, or `Get-FileHash -Algorithm SHA256` onWindows as documented. Checksums establish bytes, not a signing identity. This candidate is not cryptographically signed.

The manual publication workflow additionally downloads the actual public assets anonymously and verifies checksums with native utilities on Linux, Windows and macOS. Publication with the repository token does not trigger a separate release-event workflow. Its observed result will be appended after completion.

The local GitHub CLI upload endpoint rejected credentials with HTTP 401. Publication therefore uses the standard repository-scoped GitHub Actions token, restricted to the publication job; no credentials are embedded in source or artifacts.

## Research and limits

Exact corpus: 18 technical-document metadata observations at L1; all other six resource categories andL0/L2/L3/L4 counts are 0. Reimport recognized 18 duplicates without new records. The 1.4 million-resource goal is future work. This is not model training or fine-tuning.

Native Codex discovery remains blocked by expired client authentication; Claude/Gemini paths are documented, not executed integrations. File copying and profile syntax do not prove runtime loading. No new human preference, legal certification, native application benchmark or broad token-saving/aesthetic advantage is claimed. Adjacent procedures are implemented but product outcomes require their own evidence.
